title: Changma Xifeng Tablet alleviates Tourette syndrome by restoring striatal dopaminergic homeostasis via the C1qa/TLR4-mediated microglial polarization
authors: Ruotong Li; Yaqi Zhang; Danyang Yao; Rui Zhang; Haochen Xie; Bing Han; Hongyan Yao; Nan Sun; Jingxue Ye; Guibo Sun
evidence_type: peer-reviewed primary preclinical animal study; abstract-only extraction
date_caveat: Electronic publication and Entrez history precede prior cutoff. PubMed history October25 03:36 has unverified timezone; retrieval/indexing timing cannot be inferred from prior omission.
population: Male Sprague-Dawley rats in an IDPN-induced TS-like model, not people with Tourette.
comparator: Vehicle/model controls, formulation-only control and tiapride comparator; no verified direct comparative-effect estimate.
intervention: Changma Xifeng botanical formulation; four-week administration in rats. No human dose extrapolation.
outcome: Stereotypy, neurochemical and inflammatory markers; not clinical tic disability or quality of life.
mechanism: C1qa and related signaling changes accompanied treatment; the abstract explicitly leaves C1qa causality unresolved despite the stronger title.
adverse_events: Human safety untested here; systematic animal harms/attrition not verified.
risk_of_bias: Outcome n, blinding, attrition, multiplicity and uncertainty require full methods
Associative molecular changes do not establish mediation
claim_supported: Preclinical associations warrant qualified hypothesis status.
claim_not_supported: Human efficacy, safe self-treatment, adult or pediatric disease modification, or causal C1qa mechanism.
access: PubMed API abstract read transiently. Web-reader DOI/PubMed routes failed; full text and supplements not reviewed or stored.
reviewer: AI-assisted extraction with independent abstract check
correction_retraction_check: No linked notice in current PubMed metadata. Separate known retraction controls remain excluded.
next_verification_task: Only upgrade interpretation after lawful full methods, outcome-specific denominators/uncertainty and target-perturbation evidence; no outreach or intervention.
